item.title: Trump returns to correspondents' dinner 3 months after shooting
item.description: President Donald Trump returned to the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association dinner Friday night, delivering a rambling, hour-long speech.

item.title: Justice Department is offering billions in new grants for police who partner with ICE
item.description: The DOJ is offering state and local police $3 billion to cooperate with ICE on federal immigration enforcement, part of a broader effort to expand the administration's mass deportation campaign.

item.title: When a murder victim's son met the man wrongly convicted of the crime
item.description: Reporter Barbara Bradley Hagerty and Jay Young speak with NPR's Ailsa Chang about Young's relationship with Benjamin Spencer, the man who was wrongfully imprisoned for his father's murder.

item.title: He was falsely accused in the 1996 Atlanta Olympics bombing. How it changed his life
item.description: When a bomb exploded at the Summer Olympics in Atlanta 30 years ago, security guard Richard Jewell was named the primary suspect. His friend and attorney reflects on how that changed Jewell's life.

item.title: Community holds vigil for Wisconsin man killed by police
item.description: Hundreds of people gathered Thursday night for a vigil in Madison, Wisconsin, to remember 38-year-old Corey Ruiz. Ruiz was shot and killed by a Madison police officer in the middle of an intersection.
